summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style article on the Colt Python, a .357 Magnum revolver made by Colt's Manufacturing Company of Hartford, Connecticut. It was introduced in 1955, aimed at the premium revolver segment, and is praised by several writers and collectors as the finest production revolver ever made. The note also covers its discontinuation: Colt announced the end of production in October 1999, citing market conditions and lawsuit costs, and limited special-order production by the Colt Custom Gun Shop ended in 2005.
one_line: The Colt Python is a discontinued .357 Magnum premium revolver made by Colt in Hartford, Connecticut, from 1955 until 2005.
key_facts: The Colt Python is a .357 Magnum caliber revolver formerly manufactured by Colt's Manufacturing Company of Hartford, Connecticut.
The Colt Python is sometimes referred to as a "Combat Magnum".
The Colt Python was first introduced in 1955, the same year as Smith & Wesson's M29 .44 Magnum.
The Colt Python was intended for the premium revolver market segment.
Jeff Cooper, Ian V. Hogg, Chuck Hawks, Leroy Thompson, Scott Wolber, Renee Smeets and Martin Dougherty have described the Python as the finest production revolver ever made.
In October 1999, Colt Manufacturing Co. announced that it was ceasing production of Python revolvers.
In a 2000 follow-up letter to distributors, Colt cited changing market conditions and the costs of defending lawsuits as reasons for discontinuing the Python line.
Colt also discontinued a number of other models along with the Python line in 2000.
The Colt Custom Gun Shop continued making a limited number of Pythons on special order.
Limited special-order production of the Colt Python by the Colt Custom Gun Shop ceased in 2005.
